body.statement:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), meaning that every bounded factorwise centered additive latent score generates for all sufficiently small positive and negative path parameters a product-factor path remaining in \(\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the full observed-data tangent space satisfies \(\mathcal T=\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}^{\,L^2(P)}\).  At such a \(P\),
\[
\mathcal T^{\perp}=\{k\in L^2_0(P):E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid A,J,X)=E(k\mid Z,J,X)=0\}.
\]
body.justification: Equality with the full observed DQM closure, not merely a convenient submodel score span, is the key efficiency theorem.
body.gap: Continuous full-law recovery in Hu and Schennach and its triple-proxy causal use in Deaner are identification statements, not a measurable uniformly bounded inverse of the derivative of the factor map. The binary tangent calculation in Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen also does not establish that multilevel DQM lifting on the stated regular stratum.
body.consumer: It turns the candidate variance calculation into the information bound for every regular estimator of the smoking-level contrasts.
body.proof_tex:
By the differential-score lifting theorem, every observed DQM score belongs to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}\); closure therefore gives \(\mathcal T\subseteq\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}\).  Conversely, at the stated two-sided pathwise-interior point, every bounded factorwise centered score generates an admissible product-factor DQM path.  Its observed score is its conditional expectation given \(O\), hence belongs to \(\mathcal T\).  Truncation and factorwise recentering make bounded scores dense in each factor \(L^2\) space, while conditional expectation is an \(L^2\) contraction.  Thus \(\overline{\mathcal S_{\mathrm{lat}}}\subseteq\mathcal T\), proving equality.

For the orthocomplement, let \(k\in L^2_0(P)\).  Orthogonality to all centered outcome-factor scores is equivalent, by conditional-expectation duality, to
\[
E(k\mid Y,J,X)=E(k\mid J,X). \tag{17}
\]
The analogous conditions for the two measurement factors replace \(Y\) in (17) by \(A\) and \(Z\).  Orthogonality to all centered propensity scores makes \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)\), and orthogonality to all marginal \(X\)-scores makes \(E(k\mid X)=E(k)=0\).  Hence orthogonality to the latent additive image implies the three displayed conditional-zero restrictions.  Conversely, any one of those restrictions implies \(E(k\mid J,X)=E(k\mid X)=0\); all three together make the inner product with every factor score zero by iterated expectation.  This proves the characterization.
